question: Ticket 1e62c1529f4c says "when instance is 0 and rest[0] names a directory CLASS_ROOT/<device>/machines/<rest[0]>, step into it and drop the word; repeat while the next word names a directory under that level's machines/", but outline 5.4.3.2 reads "The launcher walks the words. `cairn cairn foo bar` (the long form) means "tell the cairn device to run foo with argument bar". At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word. Is it a script in this level's bin/? Run it, pass back the result, done. Neither? It is a bus verb: send it to this level over the bus. So `cairn foo bar baz`: foo is a device; it has a machine bar; bar's bin/ has baz, so baz runs. No bar machine? bar goes to foo over the bus. Each check is one directory lookup, so it is fast. WHY scripts first: scripts are the simple path; the bus is the route to what a device answers itself." (Outline 5.4.3.2 states "At each level: is the next word a machine here? Step into it and take the next word" without restricting to instance 0. Outline 2.3.4.2 states "Nothing in a device's code differs by instance", meaning machines exist identically for all instances. The ticket restricts the machine walk to instance 0 only, which prevents clause 5.4.3.2 from holding for instances > 0. When built exactly as written, the launcher will not check for machines at each level for instances other than 0, violating the universal requirement.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. The instance-0 limit was copied from the class_word branch; a machine is class code, the same for every instance (2.3.4.2). Revised: the walk runs for every instance, and clause 5 asserts cairn <device>.1 m go a runs the machine script.
